previous_description: A passive structure element representing a formal or informal specification of an agreement between a service provider and consumer, defining obligations, rights, and terms. Often associated with a Product or BusinessService.
definition: A business object that records an agreement between two or more parties, typically a service provider and a consumer, stating the obligations, rights, and terms (e.g., SLA levels, pricing, durations, penalties) that govern how a business service or product is delivered and used. It is information acted upon, not behavior or an actor.

distinguish_from.when: the information has business relevance but does not bind identified parties to obligations, rights, or terms (e.g., an invoice, order, or customer record)
the element is the perceptible form of the agreement, such as the signed PDF, HTML terms page, or on-screen acceptance form, rather than the agreement's content
the element is the offered bundle of services and contracts sold to a market, rather than the terms attached to it
the element is the state change of the agreement, such as a contract being signed, renewed, or terminated, rather than the agreement itself

code_evidence: A domain class or schema named Agreement, Contract, Subscription, or ServiceLevelAgreement with fields such as parties, effectiveDate, expiryDate, termsVersion, and obligations or penalties
SLA or SLO configuration files that declare uptime, response-time, or support-tier commitments bound to a named customer plan or tier
Versioned terms-of-service, license, or data-processing-agreement documents in the repository, with code that records a user's acceptance of a specific terms version

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of the agreement: the parties, the services or product it covers, and its key obligations and terms. Set it whenever the element name alone does not identify which agreement is meant.

notes: ArchiMate treats Contract as passive structure, so the outgoing serves, triggers, and accesses relationships are invalid. Passive elements are accessed; they do not act. Consider modelling Contract as a specialization of BusinessObject. It also lacks structured attributes (parties, effectiveDate, expiryDate, version) that would help classification.
